correctness.rationale: The exact all-input recurrence \(a_{2n+\rho}=a_n+\mathbb E a_B+\rho\) follows from the uniform-pair split. For \(\alpha=\log_2\varphi\), \(2^\alpha=1+2^{-\alpha}\). The global inequality \(z^\alpha\ge1+\alpha(z-1)-(z-1)^2\) proves a binomial Jensen deficit at most \((n/2)^{\alpha-1}/2\), which is <=Pr(B>0) for n>=2; n=1 is direct. Strong induction with lower (m^alpha+1)/2 and upper 2m^alpha−1 gives both even and odd cases, using \(2((2n+1)^\alpha-(2n)^\alpha)\ge2^{-n}\). Exact rational recurrence and independent exhaustive transform check match for all n<=12, and finite inequalities checked to n=150. Numeric checks are corroboration, not the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2020 Lim–Liao–Yao full manuscript proves only the logarithmic exponent limit for the identical expected-cost recurrence, not constant-factor bounds; its Section 4 explicitly calls refined behavior open. Garivier 2026 Section 8 writes the same mean recurrence and treats the exponent heuristically, while discussing a different worst-case residual-one quantity. The 2018 non-asymptotic paper focuses on numerical finite-length extraction and heuristic maximal redundancy. No searched index result or accessible previously recorded claim supplied this two-sided all-length theorem. Relative-priority risk persists.

value.rationale: The exact fair-input residual cost is a natural, central efficiency invariant of Peres extraction. Replacing an \(N^{\alpha+o(1)}\) logarithmic-exponent theorem with explicit universal multiples of \(N^\alpha\) removes the possibility of unbounded subpower corrections and provides a finite-length guarantee for every N. It complements, without conflating with, current worst-case residual sparsity research. The point is a structural, infinite all-N order classification, not a small numerical improvement or arbitrary slice.
